BKG.doc: Background flag: non-zero when the task is running as a background (ghost) task, 0 for an interactive session.

CHN.doc: Binary string listing the channels currently open (2 bytes per channel number).

CTL.doc: Control value of the key or GUI event that terminated the last INPUT/OBTAIN (e.g. 4 for F4, or a control's ctl_id for a button).

DAY.doc: Current date as a string in the DAY_FORMAT format (default "MM/DD/YY"). Can be changed with SETDAY.

DLM.doc: Directory delimiter used by the operating system ("\" on Windows, "/" on UNIX).

DSZ.doc: Data size: amount of memory (bytes) still available for data/variables.

EOM.doc: End-of-message character that terminated the last INPUT (e.g. $0D$ for Enter).

ERR.doc: Number of the last error that occurred (0 if none). Use MSG(ERR) for its text.

ERS.doc: Secondary error status for the last error (e.g. the underlying operating-system error code).

FN.doc: Prefix for user-defined functions (DEF FNname / FNname(...)); & is an alias. Not usable as a variable on its own.

GFN.doc: Returns an unused global file (channel) number from the high channel range (e.g. 65000).

GID.doc: Group identifier of the current user/process (binary string).

HFN.doc: Returns the highest unused file (channel) number (e.g. 32767); useful for opening files in utility routines without clashing with application channels.

HLP.doc: Current help reference (the help key/topic in effect for INPUT/GUI help).

HWD.doc: Home working directory: the ProvideX home/start-up directory.

LFA.doc: Last file accessed: channel number of the last file I/O operation.

LFO.doc: Last file opened: channel number used by the most recent OPEN.

LPG.doc: Last program (name of the previously executing program).

LWD.doc: Local working directory: the current working directory (see CWDIR).

MDE.doc: Current mode/environment string (not available in an embedded COM session).

MSE.doc: Mouse/event status: binary string describing the last mouse event and GUI state.

MSL.doc: Match string length: length of the text matched by the last MSK() function.

NAR.doc: Number of arguments passed to the current CALLed program, function or method.

NID.doc: Node identifier: the network/computer name of the workstation.

OBJ.doc: Object-related system value (e.g. the number of the current/last object).

PFX.doc: Current file prefix list (search directories set by PREFIX), space separated.

PGN.doc: Program name: full path of the currently executing program ("" in command mode).

PRC.doc: Current numeric precision (number of decimal places set by PRECISION; default 2).

PRM.doc: List of all system parameters and their current settings, e.g. "'BY'=0,-'AH',..." (a leading - means the parameter is off).

PSZ.doc: Program size: memory (bytes) used by the program currently loaded.

RET.doc: Return value (status code) from the last operating-system level call (e.g. SYS/INVOKE or DLL call).

RND.doc: A random number between 0 and 1 (see also the RND() function and RANDOMIZE).

SEP.doc: Default field separator character $8A$ used between fields in records.

SSN.doc: Serial number of the ProvideX licence (e.g. "0962-001-..."; the first part is the version).

TIM.doc: Current time of day in hours as a decimal number (e.g. 13.5 = 1:30 pm). Can be set with SETTIME.

TME.doc: Current time of day in hours (like TIM).

TMS.doc: Current milliseconds / sub-second part of the system time.

UID.doc: User identifier: the operating-system login name of the user.

UNT.doc: Returns the lowest unused channel number, for use in OPEN (UNT).

WHO.doc: Identifier of the workstation/terminal (e.g. the computer name).

_OBJ.doc: Inside an object method, the handle of the current object (like "this"/"self"). Outside a method it is 0.

%.doc: Global variables: any variable whose name starts with % (e.g. %COMPANY$, %USER) is global — shared by all programs in the session and not cleared by RUN/BEGIN.

$$.doc: Null (empty) hex string literal. $hex$ literals give binary strings, e.g. $0D0A$; $$ is the empty string.
